articles.title: Corey Kiner and the Best Week 10 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football playoffs are inching closer, making this a critical time to find potential difference-makers on the waiver wire.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football playoffs are inching closer, making this a critical time to find potential difference-makers on the waiver wire.

Whether you are cruising to a first-round bye and simply need backups to pad out depth or are locked into a tight battle for one of the final spots on the postseason bracket and desperately need starters who can step in to save your season, there are plenty of strong options available heading into Week 10.

There's a surprising amount of serviceable talent lingering on the free-agent scrap heap right now, especially after injuries continued to decimate rosters around the NFL over the weekend.

With that in mind, here are the top waiver-wire pickups for Week 10.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (34 Percent Rostered)

Aaron Rodgers emerged on the QB1 radar earlier in the season, posting four consecutive QB13 or better finishes before going cold for two games leading into Pittsburgh's Week 9 bye. A matchup against a middling Cincinnati Bengals defense represents an ideal opportunity for the 42-year-old to return to form.

Rodgers already had one of his best performances of 2026 against Cincy, throwing for 292 yards and a trio of touchdowns in Week 3. Another big outing could be in the works as these teams gear up to meet for the final time this regular season.

While Rodgers isn't the type of QB you want to start on a weekly basis, he's a perfect one-week rental for those dealing with injuries or byes to their regular No. 1. Don't be afraid to make him your top plug-and-play pickup for Week 10.

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (13 Percent Rostered)

J.J. McCarthy started his run as New York's QB red-hot, coming in and eviscerating the New Orleans Saints defense for 17.3 points in a single quarter. He's barely reached that many points across his first two starts combined, however, making this a bit of a risky play.

McCarthy is coming off a dreadful showing against the Philadelphia Eagles, mustering a meager 127 yards through the air and 22 on the ground while picking up a hip injury in the process. He'll look to rebound against a softer Washington Commanders foe in Week 10, a team that has given up the fifth-most points per game to opposing passers in 2026.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (34 Percent Rostered)

Malik Willis was averaging nearly 21 points over a three-game stretch spanning Weeks 5–8, but he came back down to earth in an underwhelming 19-9 defeat to the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

While Willis didn't fare well in a dream matchup against one of the league's softest defenses, he's still worth firing up against a downtrodden Indianapolis Colts squad in Week 10.

Indy has been stripping its roster down to the studs ahead of the trade deadline and has only kept one of its last four opponents under 26 points. Any manager desperate for help at the QB position can give Willis one more shot at filling their starting role.

Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (32 Percent Rostered)

Seth McGowan has the potential to be the most valuable waiver-wire addition of the 2026 NFL season.

With Jonathan Taylor's name being perhaps the most prominent in the rumor mill over the last few weeks, it would be a surprise if Indy's superstar back isn't on his way out by Tuesday evening.

Taylor's departure would immediately open the door for the seventh-round rookie to become Indianapolis' starting running back.

McGowan has already demonstrated elite potential in a backup role, recording 208 rushing yards and a touchdown on 43 carries. He offers ideal size and speed for the position and should be able to withstand the rigors of an RB1 workload, keeping fellow backup DJ Giddens largely irrelevant for fantasy purposes.

While there is some risk associated with investing in a Colts offense that has already given up key starters and could soon lose several more, McGowan has tremendous volume-based upside if Taylor is traded. He'll be a plug-and-play starter on a weekly basis with high-end RB2 upside for the remainder of the season.

Note that McGowan's value plummets if Taylor isn't moved by the deadline. If 4 p.m. ET passes with the veteran staying put, adjust your waiver priority and FAAB bids down significantly.

Corey Kiner, New England Patriots (4 Percent Rostered)

Kiner has shockingly found himself in a position where he's set to handle the majority of New England's backfield work for a stretch.

Longtime veteran Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon injury and will miss New England's upcoming matchup against the Lions in Germany. TreVeyon Henderson hasn't practiced in November and continues to miss time after experiencing neurological symptoms that required hospitalization.

Those absences leave Kiner and practice squad callup Lan Larison as the Pats' primary healthy options heading into Week 10.

Kiner took advantage of an expanded opportunity on Sunday, rushing eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown. The second-year back out of Cincinnati has already accumulated 244 rushing yards on 50 carries this season and should quickly add to that tally against a soft Detroit defense.

While a lack of receiving upside limits his ceiling in PPR formats, the opportunity to handle significant early-down work makes him a viable flex option going forward.

Audric Estime, New Orleans Saints (4 Percent Rostered)

Estime is yet another serviceable fantasy waiver wire pickup set to benefit from injuries and changes to his team's backfield rotation. With New Orleans finally moving on from Kendre Miller after several disappointing seasons, Estime stepped into a larger role and led the Saints in touches in Week 9.

Estime finished a 23-22 overtime win against the Cleveland Browns with 72 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries and tallied one reception for five yards. Although Alvin Kamara remains involved, the veteran star is clearly fading and hasn't been able to take on a consistent workload this season.

While Estime would be a slam-dunk pickup if New Orleans' backfield rotation were to remain stagnant, the potential return of Travis Etienne Jr. throws a wrench in things. Etienne is eligible to return from the IR and could be back on the field at any point in the coming weeks, making Estime a free-agent target to avoid investing too heavily into.

Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers (39 Percent Rostered)

Black is one of the very best handcuff options in fantasy football, but he's also developed into an important piece of San Francisco's backfield. Despite handling only 68 carries while working behind Christian McCaffrey in 2026, the rookie has racked up over 300 rushing yards and scored a touchdown.

Black's usage is trending upwards as the Niners look to limit McCaffrey's touches and keep him healthy for the team's upcoming postseason run. He turned in an efficient 70 yards on just 11 totes in a win over the Las Vegas Raiders this weekend. That performance gives him some flex appeal going into a Week 10 showdown against a sieve-like Dallas Cowboys defense.

Make sure Black is rostered in your league, as he's worth a bench spot in most formats as a handcuff alone. With his standalone value also growing, he's become an ideal low-risk, high-reward waiver target.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (44 Percent Rostered)

Although Flournoy failed to capitalize on an increased role in Week 9, the third-year veteran is still one of the best waiver receivers managers can hope to find during a lean week for the position.

Prior to getting bottled up by the Indianapolis Colts' secondary and turning in his first single-digit fantasy performance since Week 4, Flournoy had recorded 11 or more fantasy points in four consecutive contests.

He finished as the WR28 or better in each of those games, a string of impressive performances that proved he has the trust of quarterback Dak Prescott.

Better days should be ahead for Flournoy, especially if George Pickens remains sidelined or hindered by the hamstring injury that kept him out in Week 9.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (31 Percent Rostered)

Williams has great rest-of-season value after the Commanders adjusted their pecking order without Terry McLaurin in the picture.

The rookie was clearly the team's top choice for an increased role in the passing attack and has seen a bump in targets commensurate with this status.

While Williams hasn't done too much with the 13 looks he's received over the last two weeks, he's primed to improve on the eight catches for 79 yards he's managed to tally in that span.

He'll remain a solid No. 2 option behind Stefon Diggs and should see a big jump in production as Washington enters a soft portion of its schedule, starting with a bout against the NFC East rival New York Giants in Week 10.

Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (29 Percent Rostered)

Douglas is emerging as one of Miami's best young offensive players. While he isn't a surefire plug-and-play piece for Week 10, his ceiling gives him some sneaky strong value in deeper formats and for those managers looking to roll the dice on upside.

Although the rookie has missed several games with injury, he's been consistently productive when he has been on the field. He's posted WR26 or better finishes in three of his first five NFL games and was one of Miami's few bright spots during a 19-9 defeat to the Lions in Week 9—finishing the contest with 70 receiving yards on six receptions.

DeMario Douglas, New England Patriots (46 Percent Rostered)

Although he wasn't projected to play much of a role in New England's revamped receiving corps this season, Douglas capitalized on a series of injuries to emerge as one of Drake Maye's most consistent targets over the past month-plus.

Douglas averaged more than 70 yards per game through the air over his last five contests and scored a respectable four touchdowns during that stretch.

As long as AJ Brown remains out or limited by the litany of injuries that has plagued the start of his tenure with the organization, Douglas will remain fantasy relevant.

Expect a decent Week 10 showing against a suspect Detroit defense that has given up nearly 22 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (7 Percent Rostered)

Waller came out of nowhere to serve as Carolina's top receiving option in a Week 9 defeat to the Denver Broncos. The veteran tight end ended the contest with eight receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets, good for a whopping 23 fantasy points and a TE1 finish.

While Waller can't be expected to produce those types of eye-popping numbers on a regular basis, he should receive more than the two targets per game he averaged over the Panthers' previous three matchups.

He averaged seven targets during a two-game stretch between Weeks 3-4 and could see five-plus looks when the team heads to the Superdome to face a beatable Saints defense.

Consider Waller the best of an underwhelming crop of Week 10 tight end waiver wire targets. The 34-year-old is always a threat to score and could provide week-winning numbers if he gets hot again.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (33 Percent Rostered)

Freiermuth has been largely inconsistent in 2026, but he generated a bit of momentum going into Pittsburgh's Week 9 bye.

After two consecutive weeks with four or fewer fantasy points, the veteran turned things around with an 11.6-point outing against the rival Cleveland Browns.

Pittsburgh's opponent coming off the break, the Cincinnati Bengals, has struggled against opposing TEs in 2026 and could easily give up a touchdown to Freiermuth during the matchup.

While Freiermuth isn't the type of tight end you want to start on a weekly basis, that TD upside and stable floor are enough to warrant streaming consideration during a week when several prominent tight ends will be out on bye.

Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (18 Percent Rostered)

Tyler Higbee could be in line for an expanded role following a series of significant injuries to the Los Angeles receiving corps.

Davante Adams is still on the shelf for several more weeks, while Puka Nacua could be out even longer after suffering a concerning knee injury.

With fellow tight end Terrance Ferguson also dealing with injuries, Higbee is one of L.A.'s last remaining proven pass-catching options.

While the 33-year-old has been largely quiet outside of a stretch in which he posted three consecutive TE12-or-better finishes in Weeks 3–5, he's trending towards a resurgence late in 2026.

articles.title: Vikings' Carson Wentz Drops Honest Quote After Being on Wrong Side of NFL History With Rare Stat
articles.summary: Carson Wentz didn't even try to mince words about his performance in the Minnesota Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
Carson Wentz didn't even try to mince words about his performance in the Minnesota Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.

Speaking to reporters after throwing for 81 yards and two interceptions, Wentz described it as a "pretty terrible" outing for him.

"I haven't had many starts over the last couple of years in general, but this one felt pretty terrible," Wentz said.

Wentz completed just eight of his 25 attempts against Buffalo. ESPN added more context to how dire this game was, including him posting the worst passer rating by any quarterback since the infamous Sam Darnold "seeing ghosts" performance against the New England Patriots in 2019.

Wentz's completion percentage of 32.0 was the worst by a quarterback in a game this season with at least 10 attempts.

The Vikings started Wentz against Buffalo with Kyler Murray ruled out due to a hamstring injury suffered in Week 8.

There was some hope that Wentz could provide a boost to the passing game because he was at least able to push the ball downfield in his two appearances earlier in the season.

Two of Justin Jefferson's four touchdowns this season came in Week 1 after Wentz came in for an injured Murray.

Instead, Wentz played one of the worst games by a quarterback all season. The six points were the fewest for the Vikings since a 26-0 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 13 last season when Max Brosmer started.

The Vikings have been rumored to be in the market for a quarterback ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. The combination of Murray's injury and Wentz's struggles could lead them to get even more aggressive.

Minnesota has lost back-to-back games after a 6-0 start. As if things weren't bad enough coming out of Monday night, its next two games are on the road against the Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers.

articles.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Rankings Overview for All Positions
articles.summary: Week 9 ended with Monday night's showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. Week 10 will begin with Thursday night's matchup between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants.
articles.body:
Week 9 ended with Monday night's showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. Week 10 will begin with Thursday night's matchup between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants.

Unfortunately, injuries will again be a factor in Week 10, and Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua (knee) is the latest fantasy superstar to go down. The Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will also be on bye this week.

Who will be available and trustworthy in Week 10? Let's run down some early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings and examine a few sleepers who should be available on the waiver wire.

Sleeper: Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers

The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off their bye and are set for a pivotal matchup against the rival Cincinnati Bengals. That could mean a strong game for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

Rodgers didn't do a whole lot in Pittsburgh's last two wins, but he topped 17 fantasy points in four straight games before that. The Bengals have surrendered an average of 17.9 fantasy points to opposing QBs this season.

Rodgers is rostered in only 34 percent of fantasy leagues.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Audric Estimé, New Orleans Saints

The Cleveland Browns released Audric Estimé early last week, and the New Orleans Saints immediately brought him back. They also pushed him right into a prominent role, and it paid off.

Against Cleveland, Estimé racked up 72 rushing yards, five receiving yards, a touchdown, and 14.7 fantasy points. This week, he'll face a Carolina Panthers defense that has been better against the run recently but not great overall.

Carolina has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing RBs this season. Estimé is rostered in only seven percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Demario Douglas, New England Patriots

The New England Patriots continue to deal with injuries at wide receiver. While Mack Hollins returned in Week 9, A.J. Brown was out, and Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve.

New England's receiver situation has, however, created opportunities for Demario Douglas. He has topped 15 fantasy points in back-to-back games and in four of his last five. This week, he'll face the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered an average of 28.5 fantasy points to opposing receiving corps.

Douglas is still only rostered in 36 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers

Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker struggled to find open space against the Denver Broncos' vaunted defense on Sunday. However, Carolina was able to find a spark by utilizing its tight ends. Darren Waller led the Panthers with eight catches, 90 yards, and a touchdown.

Waller finished with a season-high 23 fantasy points.

While Waller might not be as heavily utilized this week, he'll have a great opportunity against New Orleans. The Saints have surrendered the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing TEs. Waller is rostered in just 10 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Inside the Huddle: Jacksonville Jaguars show they are all in on Super Bowl charge with trades for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux
articles.summary: Join Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds, Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter each week on Inside the Huddle as they break down the biggest stories from around the league; the NFL returns to Germany on Sunday as the Lions face the Patriots in Munich, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm
articles.body:
Jacksonville bolstered their defense on Monday by trading for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.

Liam Coen's side sit 6-2 at the top of the AFC South and are on course for another playoff season while boasting the fourth-best scoring offense and second best scoring defense in football.

"They are doing something that is not been typical of the Jaguars. I think this might be Tony Boselli's fingerprints we're starting to see on that franchise a little bit," said Reinebold on the latest episode of Inside the Huddle.

"They're all in. They're pushing. You go out and you sign Jessie Bates and he's in an expiring contract. What that says to every guy in that locker room is, hey, Shad Khan ain't playing games no more.

"This coach we got in Liam Coen, he ain't playing. They want to win a Super Bowl - they don't just want to win, they want to win a Super Bowl. And those things can be catalysts in your locker room and to your football team."

The Jags spent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to acquire Davis from the Eagles, reuniting him with former Georgia college teammate Travon Walker.

Davis signed a three-year $78m extension with the Eagles back in March after a standout 2025 campaign, and departs an Eagles team that has lost seven straight games.

"Jordan's impact on the field can be felt on every down," said Jaguars general manager James Gladstone. "This is a well-rounded premier player and person. We're excited to add him to the team."

articles.title: “Players were texting me to get back to work”: Dianna Russini’s The Russini Report comeback could spell trouble for New England Patriots HC Mike Vrabel amid Sedona scandal controversy
articles.summary: The last six months have not been easy for Dianna Russini.
articles.body: The last six months have not been easy for Dianna Russini. From her own family to her 94-year-old grandmother, cousins, and relatives she had not spoken to in years - everyone was affected by the alleged Sedona cheating scandal involving New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.At the beginning, it was a “nightmare.” Later, as she put it, the “lies became so out of control,” that the situation felt like a runaway train. The narratives were getting out of hand, and she felt helpless.For someone who was never without her phone, even while driving, and was constantly looking for the next big scoop, she decided to step away from the news cycle. She deleted her social media accounts and focused on healing.It had become too much for her to bear. Amid this heartbreaking period, however, she found hope in text messages reportedly sent by players encouraging her to return to work.“I felt like players were texting and calling me to say, ‘Get back to work, it’s time,’” she told PEOPLE. “I think it’s pretty poetic that here I was all these years telling the story about these players going through adversity, and then they became sort of the people that I was learning from during this.”Dianna Russini returns with The Russini Report amid Mike Vrabel controversyFor the past 15 years, it has been hard to imagine the league without Dianna Russini’s reporting. She has delivered inside scoops that few others could ever get their hands on.Her rare ability to connect with players on a personal level, and others across the league, helped her develop relationships that often translated into exclusive updates and breaking news.Fans and followers would wait for her latest reports. But now with the 2026 NFL season underway, Russini has been missing from the reporting scene. Much like the injured players who work their way back to the gridiron after brutal injuries, she is making her own comeback from a brutal time.And that too at the right time - when the big games are about to begin - Russini is returning to her reporting field [sports journalism] with The Russini Report.This is a one-hour show that will stream on BetUS TV’s website and X account beginning Wednesday, November 11, 2026. She will also write an accompanying column to the series, which will air every Wednesday at 12 PM ET. Isn’t that the same day as Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights podcast?Russini Report vs New Heights - Wednesday NFL showdown?Dianna Russini’s Wednesday show will air just hours after Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights podcast releases its weekly episodes. The Kelce brothers’ episodes are available on YouTube at 5:30 AM ET every Wednesday.Each New Heights episode usually runs for about one to two hours. So, while Wednesday mornings belong to the Kelce brothers, Russini will take over the afternoon NFL conversation.After dedicating 15 years to ESPN and The Athletic, she is now returning with a show of her own, promising to share her unfiltered thoughts. “It’s really going to be a show about everything I know that’s going on in the NFL,” she said. “Along with a lot of my opinions.”That could mean discussing subjects she previously had little opportunity to address, offering perspectives she could not share in her earlier roles, and bringing a unique dimension to her reporting.In many ways, this could be Dianna Russini 2.0. A version of the reporter audiences have not seen before. Maybe not even New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Perhaps the biggest question surrounding her comeback involves the coach.Could Dianna Russini’s comeback affect Mike Vrabel?When people predicted before the 2026 season that Dianna Russini would return with a platform of her own, one that could potentially affect Mike Vrabel’s season, this is the moment they were talking about.Now, the head coach’s off-field life could start affecting his on-field responsibilities. His team has already suffered four losses while recording just five wins.If Russini’s reporting starts spilling the beans about their personal life, it could bring revamped attention to the alleged Sedona cheating controversy.Or maybe she will choose not to discuss those matters, as doing so could affect her as well. But if she never intended to revisit the subject, what would be the point of making a comeback from all that heartbreaking experience?Either way, if her stories start affecting Mike Vrabel, they could have an impact on his season. And if his team struggles, he could be the one facing the blame.And when January arrives, we all know what happens to some NFL coaches in the first week of the new year - they get fired! Anyhow. All of this is speculation for now. articles.title: Jerry Jones Teases Cowboys' Updated NFL Trade Plans Hours Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says fans shouldn't "count out" the idea his team could add a player ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says fans shouldn't "count out" the idea his team could add a player ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

"But I don't expect us to make a significant trade today," Jones said in a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan .

When asked if the Cowboys planned to make a move to replace injured running back Tyler Goodson, Jones said "we will do that today" but added the move would likely be made through free agency.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday both Goodson and tight end Jake Ferguson will miss "multiple weeks" due to knee injuries.

One running back who recently hit the free agent market is Kendre Miller, who was released last weekend by the New Orleans Saints.

The Cowboys recently sparked trade speculation by ruling out wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was acquired via trade earlier this season, ahead of a Sunday win at the Indianapolis Colts.

Jones said Tuesday the absences of both Pickens and Porter were "100 percent injury-related."

"Put it to rest," Jones said about speculation regarding other reasons for absences from Pickens and Porter.

Jones also pointed to injuries when describing roster depth with which he said he was "pretty pleased" with heading into the trade deadline.

"I'm sure a critic could look at it and say, 'How about a little more rush. How about a little more pressure. How about a little more help in the flat,'" Jones said.

"But overall, I would say we've had our depletion from injuries. We've had it at linebacker and we've had it at secondary. I'm pretty pleased with what we've done at the interior of our line, and I like the options we have at pass rush."

The Cowboys improved to 4-5 with last weekend's win against the Colts and now sit 2.5 games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

Dallas will hope to make a push to overtake the Giants down the stretch after depleting their 2027 draft stock to just four picks in order to construct their current roster.

articles.title: Brian Thomas Jr.'s Jaguars Future Revealed in New NFL Trade Rumors at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to stick with Brian Thomas Jr. despite his usage dropping off this season, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to stick with Brian Thomas Jr. despite his usage dropping off this season, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Tuesday.

According to Fowler, the Jaguars plan to keep Thomas past the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline and "have relayed that to interested teams."

Thomas had been connected to teams in need of receiver help, including the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kansas City Chiefs and Washington Commanders.

The Jaguars also previously reportedly turned down "significant" offers for Thomas ahead of the 2025 trade deadline, per The Athletic's Jeff Howe .

The news comes after the Jaguars stacked their roster for a potential playoff run in a series of Monday trades for safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux.

Thomas, who turned 24 in October, is signed through the 2027 season on a rookie contract that features a club option for 2028.

He has recorded 10 catches on 22 targets for 117 yards with two touchdowns through the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

A first-round pick out of LSU in 2024, Thomas started his career with a strong rookie season during which he recorded 87 catches for 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns in 17 games.

He took a step back during a sophomore 2025 season, making 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games.

Thomas' standing with the Jaguars seemingly declined since then as Trevor Lawrence turned more regularly to Parker Washington, Brenton Strange and Jakobi Meyers as his top targets.

Although the Jags seemingly gained enough positional depth to consider moving on from Thomas, head coach Liam Coen is apparently sticking with his previous assurances the Jaguars are committed to developing the former first-rounder.

Coen could now hope to improve Thomas' fit in the Jaguars' scheme down the stretch as Lawrence and his team look to build on their 6-2 start by securing the AFC South title.

articles.summary: It appears that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is getting closer to returning to the field.
articles.body:
It appears that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is getting closer to returning to the field.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Tuesday that Aiyuk passed his physical with the San Francisco 49ers and has officially been reinstated. He will now seek a release from the 49ers, and Schultz noted that "at least one NFC team has internally discussed the possibility of adding Aiyuk to its practice squad if and when that happens."

Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, hinted at where the wide receiver might sign as a free agent if he's released by San Francisco:

Per ESPN's Nick Wagoner , the NFL transaction wire stated that the 49ers received a two-game roster exemption to sort through any remaining business with Aiyuk before it expires on Monday, Nov. 23, after the team's Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.

Aiyuk was on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list since last December after the team voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation while he recovered from knee injuries suffered in October 2024. Despite the impending end of the ongoing saga, head coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed Aiyuk's reinstatement.

"It means absolutely nothing to our team," Shanahan said. "I think we got two-week roster exemption and that's all administrative stuff to me."

Aiyuk and his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, met with the 49ers on Friday, and Shanahan said he couldn't "care less" about what happened in the meeting. The wideout provided a brief statement to reporters.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk said. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."

The 49ers have until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday to try to trade Aiyuk, but it's hard to imagine any team giving up assets to acquire him. It's likely that San Francisco will release the 28-year-old at some point over the next two weeks, giving him the chance to resurrect his career elsewhere.

articles.title: Why Bengals 'Called Off' Trade with Eagles Revealed in New NFL Rumors at Deadline
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals reportedly backed out of a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles that would've seen them acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals reportedly backed out of a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles that would've seen them acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Bengals "called off this trade with an eye toward keeping a future comp pick they would've lost with this deal."

NFL cap expert Nick Korte explained that Cincinnati would've lost the 2027 third-round comp pick they received after edge rusher Trey Hendrickson signed with the Baltimore Ravens this past offseason.

This wasn't the first time Korte's keen eye potentially influenced a transaction. According to ESPN's Field Yates , Korte noticed in 2024 "that the Bengals appeared to be shorted a 3rd round compensatory pick following the departure of Jessie Bates in free agency. Days later, the NFL announced it had made an error and Cincinnati wound up with a 3rd round compensatory pick."

Ebiketie joined Philadelphia over the offseason after spending the first four years of his career with the Atlanta Falcons. He appeared in all nine games for the 2-7 Eagles this season and recorded 25 total tackles with no sacks. He produced 16.5 sacks during his tenure in Atlanta.

Despite his lack of production in Philadelphia, Ebiketie would've been a solid fit with the Bengals. ESPN's Ben Baby noted that Cincinnati "was looking to add an edge rusher to bolster a defensive line that recently lost one of its best players" after rookie defensive end Cashius Howell was placed on injured reserve due to a wrist injury. Adding Ebiketie would've provided some extra depth to a defense that ranks 25th in the NFL with 354.9 yards allowed per game.

Instead, the Bengals will have to search elsewhere for some defensive help before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. At 6-2, Cincinnati appears to be one of the top contenders in the AFC this season, so the team will have to shore up any holes if it hopes to represent the conference in the Super Bowl.

Bengals fans will surely be watching closely to see if any other moves are attempted before the trade deadline.

articles.title: New Vikings Trade Rumors on Kirk Cousins, Derek Carr Links amid QB Search at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: After a disastrous outing for Carson Wentz on Monday Night Football, the Minnesota Vikings' search for help at quarterback could be centered around a reunion with Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
After a disastrous outing for Carson Wentz on Monday Night Football, the Minnesota Vikings' search for help at quarterback could be centered around a reunion with Kirk Cousins.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Cousins has been identified as a "prime trade candidate" for Minnesota ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline.

This comes on the heels of Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio reporting the Vikings have not had any conversations with the New Orleans Saints about a potential deal for Derek Carr, who remains on the reserve/retired list.

Per NFL insider Dianna Russini , the Vikings also checked in with the San Francisco 49ers about Mac Jones, but the Niners' "price is too high right now."

Carr, who retired in May 2025, said in July on NFL Network's Good Morning Football he would consider a "special situation" to return to play.

"I'll never say never. It would take a special situation," Carr said (h/t NFL.com's Kevin Patra ). "There were multiple teams that reached out to me this offseason, and I won't say who or how, but they reached out. Just gave them my interest on what I wanted to do and all those things. They were good, solid football teams, but a couple of them in some different situations."

The Saints still have Carr's contractual rights, so Minnesota would have to negotiate a trade if he were even interested in playing again.

Cousins' situation with the Las Vegas Raiders is fascinating because the team has been adamant about wanting Fernando Mendoza to spend this season learning behind the scenes before taking over as the starter in 2027.

Raiders owner Mark Davis said as recently as last week there is "absolutely no pressure whatsoever" to get Mendoza on the field.

"I'm really happy with the way it is with Fernando right now," Davis added.

It can be argued the Raiders would be better served seeing what Mendoza can do right now so they know specific areas he needs to improve in the offseason.

There's also the fact that the Raiders are reeling right now following a surprise 3-0 start to the season. They have lost five of their last six games and the defense ranks last in the NFL in points allowed per game.

Cousins is coming off arguably his worst game of the season with three interceptions in a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but he has been solid overall with 2,340 passing yards and 20 touchdowns in nine games.

Minnesota is facing its first real adversity of the season coming off a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Its the second straight defeat for the team after a 6-0 start.

Wentz, who got the start in place of an injured Kyler Murray, finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions against a Buffalo defense that has been the eighth-worst in the NFL by success rate this season.

A healthy Murray hasn't really stabilized the Vikings' quarterback situation like they hoped. He ranks 27th out of 31 qualified quarterbacks in QBR and success rate.

Cousins would be a natural fit for the Vikings because he spent six seasons in Minnesota from 2018 to '23, with the last two years coming after Kevin O'Connell was hired as head coach.

The Vikings have 10 picks in the 2027 NFL draft, including two in the third round thanks to the Jonathan Greenard trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.title: Did a tweet save the Bengals from embarrassing and costly trade with Eagles?
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals nearly made a potentially disastrous trade just hours ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals nearly made a potentially disastrous trade just hours ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Early Tuesday, it was reported the Bengals agreed to trade for Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Initial reports suggested the Bengals would give up a sixth-round draft pick in the deal.

Since Ebiketie was signed as a compensatory free agent by the Eagles last offseason, the Bengals would actually forfeit a third-round compensatory pick if the trade went through. In other words, the Bengals were about to give up a sixth-round pick and lose a compensatory third-round pick in exchange for Ebiketie, a much steeper cost than the team likely anticipated.

This was pointed out on X by numerous analysts, and the trade subsequently fell through, with reporters citing that exact issue as the reason the Bengals reneged on the deal.

If you're curious about what the heck happened here, buckle up. Compensatory draft pick rules aren't the easiest to parse.

Essentially, compensatory picks are draft selections given to a team that loses a significant player or coach.

Here's how Over the Cap defines a compensatory pick:

They serve as a mechanism to reward teams for losing players to free agency, particularly those who sign significant contracts elsewhere. These picks are awarded in rounds 3 through 7 and are calculated based on a complex formula considering the salary, playing time, and postseason honors of the players lost and gained. Understanding how these picks work can provide valuable insight into team building strategies and the value placed on free agents across the league.

The Bengals were awarded a third-round compensatory pick in the 2027 NFL Draft after defensive end Trey Hendrickson left in free agency.

The team initially earned three compensatory picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, but it lost two of them after signing two other players in free agency that were designated as compensatory free agents. Because of that, the Bengals' third-round compensatory pick was the only one the team still held heading into Tuesday.

Why would Arnold Ebiketie cost the Bengals a third-round pick?

Under NFL rules, players acquired in-season via trade count toward the compensatory formula, according to ESPN's Field Yates. That's arguably the most important thing to know about this deal.

Since Ebiketie was designated as a compensatory free agent, the Bengals would assume that cost in Tuesday's trade. Because of that, the Bengals would have lost their only remaining compensatory pick — the third-rounder the team received when Hendrickson left — if they brought in a third compensatory player.

Analyst Nick Korte was credited with being the individual who first called attention to the issue on X.

That detail would have drastically altered the deal for the Bengals.

Why did the Bengals pull out of the Arnold Ebiketie deal?

When the trade was initially reported, it appeared the team believed this was the deal it was making:

• Bengals acquire: Edge Arnold Ebiketie from Eagles • Eagles acquire: A 2027 sixth-round pick from the Bengals

Once more details came to light, here was the deal the Bengals were actually about to make:

• Bengals acquire: Edge Arnold Ebiketie and assume his compensatory pick cost from Eagles • Bengals forfeit: A 2027 third-round compensatory pick • Eagles acquire: A 2027 sixth-round pick from the Bengals and offload Ebiketie's compensatory cost

Upon realizing a third-round pick was about to be taken away from them, the Bengals very quickly nixed the trade, much to the chagrin of the Eagles. While both teams had reached an agreement on the trade, it was not finalized when the Bengals called it off.

He's the self-proclaimed "Compensatory Picks Guy™."

Korte is an Over the Cap contributor and an individual seemingly obsessed with NFL contracts and compensatory draft picks. Turns out, that's a useful skill to have on NFL trade deadline day.

It's not the first time Korte has stepped in to correct a compensatory salary cap issue in the NFL. Incredibly, that situation also dealt with the Bengals and a third-round pick.

In 2024, Korte noticed the Bengals should have received a third-round compensatory pick after losing safety Jessie Bates III in free agency. The team was initially set to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick for losing Bates.

Korte pointed that out on X and the NFL actually stepped in, eventually awarding the Bengals with a third-round compensatory pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings called out "delusional" fans in a pair of social media posts.

articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have reportedly traded wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a sixth-round draft pick, per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Allen offers immediate help to a 49ers' wide receiver room that has unfortunately been hit hard with injuries.

WR (Z and Slot): Deebo Samuel Sr., Keenan Allen, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jordan Watkins

articles.title: Amani Hooker Traded to Bills From Titans, New NFL Rumors on 2026 Deadline Deal
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills reportedly bolstered their defense ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills reportedly bolstered their defense ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that the Bills acquired safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans. ESPN's Adam Schefter added that Buffalo gave up a second-round draft pick and received a fifth-round pick in the deal.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that prior to dealing for Hooker, the Bills "made a very strong push" for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.

A 2019 fourth-round pick, Hooker had spent his entire career in Tennessee. His fellow draft classmate Jeffery Simmons was also shipped away this season, with the Titans sending the standout defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears.

Hooker is tied for the league lead with five interceptions this year, giving him 17 picks for his career. He's also added 52 total tackles and six passes defended this season.

Hooker is an immediate upgrade for the Bills, who have a combined total of six interceptions through eight games. Buffalo added veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson over the offseason, but his disappointing tenure included a one-game suspension and subpar play before he was released earlier this month. If Hooker lives up to expectations, he could be the missing piece that puts the team over the top as title contenders.

The Bills already appear to be the favorites to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, improving to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football . Buffalo's struggling defense has benefited from facing backup quarterbacks in back-to-back weeks, and it will have another easy outing on Sunday against the 2-7 New York Jets.

articles.title: Tom Brady admits to more motivation after Deflategate suspension, reveals what he did while away from Patriots
articles.summary: Tom Brady revealed how he spent his Deflategate suspension on vacation before returning to lead the Patriots' legendary 28-3 Super Bowl comeback.
articles.body: Entering the 2016 season, Tom Brady had won just one Super Bowl in the last decade-plus, and then came the biggest hit of his career. Deflategate had finally settled, and the then-New England Patriots quarterback was hit with a four-game suspension for his involvement in the scandal. Outside of his torn ACL in 2008, it was the only time Brady had ever been off the football field. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Despite being in unfamiliar territory, Brady, though, took advantage of what his former teammates Julian Edelman and Rob Gronkowski joked was his "vacation." "It was a great September," Brady admitted on "The Gronk & Jules Show." Brady went back home to Pebble Beach to see his parents, took in a Michigan game, his alma mater, with his son, and went on an Italy trip with his then-wife. "I really took advantage of September. I was like, s---, I haven't had a September off since before I started playing in elementary school." TONY ROMO RESURFACES ON ALTERNATE 'MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL' TELECAST AND SHOWS HE'S BETTER THAN TROY AIKMAN But once the calendar flipped to October, and Brady returned from his ban, Brady had one thing on his mind. "I was there to whoop some a--," he said. When asked by Edelman if he had any extra motivation because of the punishment, he quickly said, "Hell yeah." "We all came back, and we all had something to prove," he added. "We always have something to prove. Every time you take the field as a competitor, you got something to prove. Mostly, you gotta prove it to yourself. What am I capable of doing, what are my teammates counting on me to do, and how do I go achieve it? And then, how can I be the best I can be for them?" Brady went 11-1 as the starter in that regular season, and that campaign was capped off with the unforgettable 28-3 comeback in the Super Bowl against the Atlanta Falcons. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Brady would win two more Super Bowls after that - one with the Pats and his seventh with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Set to Be Raiders' QB1 After Kirk Cousins Trade to Vikings at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: It's officially Fernando Mendoza time in Sin City.
articles.body:
It's officially Fernando Mendoza time in Sin City.

The 2026 No. 1 overall pick is set to make his first career start for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday after veteran Kirk Cousins was dealt to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday.

Las Vegas started the season with three straight wins before losing five of its next six games. Mendoza briefly saw action in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots, completing six of his eight passes for 48 yards in his professional debut. First-year head coach Klint Kubiak said after the team's Week 7 loss to the Los Angeles Rams that he would evaluate "everything," including the quarterback position, but he ultimately stuck with Cousins for two more weeks.

The 38-year-old veteran threw for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. Now, Mendoza will take over a Raiders offense that ranks eighth in the NFL with 26.4 points per game.

Mendoza is coming off a dream senior season at Indiana in which he won the Heisman Trophy and led the Hoosiers to an undefeated record and the national championship. He played in all three of Las Vegas' preseason games over the summer and threw one touchdown and two interceptions.

Mendoza's first start will come against a Seattle team that ranks first in total defense with 244.2 yards allowed per game. The rookie will try to get his career started on the right foot as the Raiders try to remain in the playoff race in the AFC.

Following Sunday's game against Seattle, Mendoza will face the Denver Broncos in Week 11 and Cleveland Browns in Week 12 before Vegas heads on its bye in Week 13.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Traded to Vikings From Raiders, Full Details Revealed in Latest NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings added a familiar face on the trade market.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings added a familiar face on the trade market.

The Vikings acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick on Tuesday, the team announced. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer was first to report the news.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Cousins was the "focal point" of Minnesota's search for a quarterback, with head coach Kevin O'Connell making it "very clear to ownership" that the veteran passer was the team's top target.

According to Schultz , the Vikings also inquired about the Los Angeles Chargers' Justin Herbert, Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones and New York Jets' Geno Smith before acquiring Cousins.

"The Colts listened but did not want to move Jones, while the Jets felt Smith was too important to the team and the development of other players," Schultz wrote.

"The Chargers, I'm told, immediately shut down all inquiries for Herbert, who also has a no-trade clause."

Cousins previously played for the Vikings from 2018-23.

Minnesota's interest in the 38-year-old was evident leading up to the swap, as ESPN's Adam Schefter reported earlier on Tuesday that the team identified Cousins as "a prime trade candidate."

Minnesota opened the 2026 season with a 6-0 record and still sits at 6-2, although the team had dealt with inconsistency from the quarterback position.

Kyler Murray started six games for the Vikings this year, but only compiled an 86.6 passer rating and is currently sidelined due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain .

Backup Carson Wentz started Minnesota's matchup with the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, but struggled mightily throughout the 23-6 loss. Wentz finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions.

The Vikings will hope for more stability under center with Cousins back in the mix, as he earned three Pro Bowl nods across his six seasons on the team. He also helped Minnesota make two playoff appearances.

This year, Cousins has completed 64.1 percent of his throws for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns compared to eight interceptions. He's been a key piece of a Las Vegas offense that ranks No. 8 in the NFL by averaging 26.4 points per game.

For the Raiders, they'll now turn to rookie Fernando Mendoza at quarterback after losing five of their past six games following a 3-0 start to the season.

Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, has appeared in one contest as a reserve this year. He's completed six of his eight pass attempts for 48 yards.

Mendoza also suited up in three preseason games, throwing for 240 yards and one touchdown while getting picked off twice.

articles.title: Vikings, Raiders Updated Depth Charts, Salary Cap After Kirk Cousins Trade at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have seen enough of Carson Wentz.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have seen enough of Carson Wentz.

That's one obvious conclusion after they swung a trade to reunite with Kirk Cousins, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , a day after a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

The Las Vegas Raiders, meanwhile, are paving the way for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to become the starting quarterback.

Here's what each team looks like at the skill positions following the deal:

QB: Kirk Cousins, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer, Kyler Murray (inj.)

RB: Jordan Mason, Aaron Jones Sr., DeeJay Dallas

RB: Ashton Jeanty, Mike Washington Jr., Dylan Laube

WR: Tre Tucker, Cody White, Malik Benson

TE: Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas

Cousins signed a one-year deal with the Raiders but could remain on the books for Minnesota in 2027 thanks to a $10 million club option.

The Vikings had to do something to address their QB situation before Tuesday's deadline. Kyler Murray is nursing a hamstring issue, and his performance was disappointing prior to the injury.

Things got worse Monday night as Wentz and Max Brosmer combined to throw for 127 yards and two interceptions.

Minnesota's defense can only carry the team so far. The offense needed an upgrade under center, and Cousins should be just that. He threw for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in his nine starts with the Raiders.

The Raiders, meanwhile, were having a hard time keeping up the facade they could contend for the playoffs. They've lost five of their last six games. The handover to Mendoza was inevitable.

The Cousins signing worked out as well as Las Vegas could've hoped in what was a reset year. Flipping him for a Day 2 draft pick is almost the best-case scenario.

ESPN's Ryan McFadden floated the idea the team could wait until after its Week 13 bye to name Mendoza the starter because the schedule gets a little easier over the final month.

Assuming Mendoza is the new QB1, he'll line up Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, who are allowing the fewest passing yards in the league. The Cleveland Browns, who are sixth in pass defense, await in Week 12.

Don't be surprised if Mendoza looks a little shaky out of the gate because he's facing quite a learning curve.

articles.title: New Justin Herbert Trade Rumors on Vikings Links Surface After Kirk Cousins Deal at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins reportedly wasn't the only quarterback the Minnesota Vikings targeted ahead of the trade deadline.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins reportedly wasn't the only quarterback the Minnesota Vikings targeted ahead of the trade deadline.

The Vikings also looked into a potential deal for the Los Angeles Chargers' Justin Herbert, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Tuesday.

According to Schultz, the Chargers "immediately shut down all inquiries for Herbert."

The Vikings also asked about the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones and New York Jets' Geno Smith before trading Tuesday for Cousins, according to Schultz.

The Vikings reportedly acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick.

Schultz reported Cousins was the "focal point" of the Vikings' search for a quarterback.

"Kevin O'Connell made it very clear to ownership that [Cousins] was the No. 1 target, per multiple league sources," Schultz reported.

This isn't the first time the Vikings have been connected to Herbert. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the franchise reached out to the Chargers about a potential trade ahead of the 2025 season but were met with "a flat no."

The latest trade rumors come after Herbert went from a 2025 Pro Bowl campaign to the worst season start of his career.

The Chargers have gone 0-8 as Herbert has completed a personal-low 61.3 percent of his passes and thrown just six touchdowns while getting picked off an NFL-high 11 times.

The Vikings could have been hoping a change of scenery would allow Herbert to bounce back down the stretch, although the Chargers quarterback would have to be on board. Herbert is signed through the 2029 season on a deal that reportedly features a no-trade clause.

The Chargers would also have to be willing to take on a $72.8 million in dead cap this season by trading Herbert, per Over the Cap .

The Vikings are instead turning to a familiar option under center. O'Connell and Cousins worked together in Minnesota for two seasons, including the quarterback's most recent Pro Bowl campaign in 2022.

Minnesota has been through multiple starters since Cousins left after the 2023 season, including a successful 2024 run with Sam Darnold and a less consistent 2025 campaign behind J.J. McCarthy.

The Vikings committed to Kyler Murray as QB1 before trading McCarthy to the Giants this season, only to lose Murray on a week-to-week basis to a hamstring strain.

The move to trade for Cousins comes after Carson Wentz posted one of the worst-rated quarterback performances in recent NFL history during a 23-6 Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills

The Vikings will hope granting O'Connell's apparent wish by reuniting him with Cousins will give this team enough offensive depth to take advantage of its dominant defense and make a playoff run this winter.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson, Kirk Cousins' Updated Vikings Fantasy Outlook After QB's Trade from Raiders
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are reportedly turning back to a familiar face, and that is excellent news for fantasy football managers counting on Justin Jefferson to carry their roster.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are reportedly turning back to a familiar face, and that is excellent news for fantasy football managers counting on Justin Jefferson to carry their roster.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for quarterback Kirk Cousins.

The trade comes after Kyler Murray missed Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills with a hamstring injury and Carson Wentz performed terribly in his place while going 8-of-25 for 81 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions.

It's not as if Murray was playing well before the setback either, as he had just five touchdown passes to three interceptions through his first six games.

Those who selected Jefferson highly in their fantasy drafts know all about the quarterback struggles for the Vikings, and the Cousins trade should offer them plenty of reason for optimism. After all, Cousins performed at a high level statistically for the Raiders this season while completing 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

He has never been hesitant to air it out downfield, and there is already a chemistry in place from his previous time on the Vikings when Jefferson was also his No. 1 option.

In fact, Cousins threw for more than 4,.000 yards in three consecutive seasons from 2020 through 2022 when he and Jefferson anchored the aerial attack in Minnesota.

Jefferson is averaging a career-worst 56.1 receiving yards per game this season catching passes from Murray and Wentz, so there should be an immediate uptick in his production. While fantasy managers were undoubtedly starting him every week anyway given his status as one of the best receivers in the league, he has largely underperformed.

Now they have every reason to believe he will live up to expectations moving forward.

As for Cousins, he is also an underrated fantasy threat. While he may not be in the same discussion as quarterbacks such as Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, he is second in the league in passing touchdowns and fifth in passing yards.

All of that production was in Las Vegas where his top weapon was a tight end in Brock Bowers. Jefferson and Jordan Addison give him more vertical threats in the passing game that will help him air it out even more and continue to put up impressive fantasy numbers.

At this point, Cousins is a fantasy starter even if he wasn't a high draft pick.

The Vikings are also in a much better position to make a run toward the Super Bowl with their dominant defense now that they have a much higher ceiling at the quarterback position following this trade.

articles.title: Grade the trade: Vikings get a throwback QB, deal with Raiders for old friend Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: The Raiders got a valuable pick for a QB who was likely to be benched soon.
articles.body:
After Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings knew they had to try to get a quarterback.

The Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins , who spent six of his 15 NFL seasons in Minnesota. They sent a third-round pick to the Raiders for the 38-year-old quarterback, via ESPN .

That should start the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas, while giving the Vikings hope for fixing their offense and winning the NFC North.

Usually, viable quarterbacks aren't available in trade. Credit to the Vikings for getting a deal done.

After Minnesota watched Carson Wentz flounder around on Monday night , and after the team realized Kyler Murray wouldn't be the answer, a bold move was needed. Cousins has played pretty well this season, with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He can come right in and run Kevin O'Connell's offense, which made him more valuable to Minnesota than some other teams.

The Vikings weren't going to be a Super Bowl contender with a treacherous quarterback situation. Cousins might not completely change that — he's still by far the fourth-best quarterback in a tough division — but it's well worth the price of a third-round pick to find out.

The Raiders played the Kirk Cousins/Fernando Mendoza situation perfectly, as it turns out.

They paid Cousins and gave him the first nine games of the season. With the Raiders slipping to 4-5 and their playoff hopes becoming more unrealistic, it was about time to turn the offense over to Mendoza anyway. So the Raiders paid for half of a season from Cousins and got a third-round pick out of it in the end. That's really smart business.

The Raiders might have Aidan O'Connell start for a few games if they truly don't think Mendoza, the first overall pick, is ready. Either way, Las Vegas was playing chess with how it got a valuable top-100 pick for a 38-year-old quarterback who was probably going to start only a few more games anyway.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins: Minnesota Vikings reportedly re-sign quarterback from Las Vegas Raiders
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have reportedly re-signed Kirk Cousins in a deal with the Las Vegas Raiders; The Raiders will receive a 2027 third-round pick; Cousins was originally with the Vikings from 2018 until 2023
articles.body:
Cousins spent six years with the Vikings from 2018-2023 before he left to join the Atlanta Falcons as a free agent in 2024.

The Vikings have since struggled to find a replacement for him and have eight quarterbacks start since his move.

It means that the 2026 No 1 pick Carlos Mendoza will now be the starting quarterback for the Raiders and the Las Vegas outfit have also received a 2027 third-round pick for the trade.

The Vikings had an extra third-round selection from Philadelphia in a swap they made in April for edge rusher Jonathan Greenard.

The deal comes less than 24 hours after a dire performance for Carson Wentz as he put in the worst performance by a quarterback at the franchise since 2006 in the absence of usual starter Kyler Murray, who is out with a hamstring injury. Not only that, the Vikings are on a losing run after a 6-2 start.

Wentz was 8 for 25 for 81 yards, two interceptions and a lost fumble from a badly overthrown swing pass to Justin Jefferson in the first quarter that went backward for a live ball. With Wentz hobbling on an ankle injury and the offense going nowhere, Max Brosmer took over midway through the fourth quarter of the 23-6 loss.

Cousins had some of his best performances with the Vikings while helping them win 13 games in 2022 in coach Kevin O'Connell's first season, and he was playing even better in 2023 when he tore his Achilles tendon during a game at Green Bay in Week 8.

Now, the Vikings have made a major move to try to keep their season on track with a dominant defence and plenty of capable pieces on offense around the quarterback.

articles.title: Colts reportedly turned down second-round picks to keep RB Jonathan Taylor
articles.summary: Per the report, Indianapolis turned down multiple offers of second-round picks to keep Taylor in a Colts uniform.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts were aggressive sellers at the trade deadline.

But the most prominent potential trade piece on their roster is staying put. Per NFL Insider Tom Pelissero , the Colts declined to trade three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.

Per the report, Indianapolis turned down multiple offers of second-round picks to keep Taylor in a Colts uniform. The Colts would have only considered a "blockbuster" return to part with Taylor, according to the report.

It's a curious decision for a team that's given up on the season and faces what looks like a long road back to relevance.

Taylor has been one of the league's most reliable and productive backs throughout his seven-season NFL career. At 27 years old — toward the end of the traditional running-back prime — he's a potential difference-maker for a team seeking to compete for a championship now. The Colts are not that and don't project to be anytime soon.

But Taylor has been the face of the Colts through most of his career and is a fan favorite. That holds value in Indianapolis, so much that the Colts reportedly turned down multiple reasonable offers that would have provided a valuable asset to build for the future.

Fire sale after Chris Ballard's dismissal

Amid the failures of extending Daniel Jones and trading two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner, the Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard in October after a 2-4 start. This triggered a fire sale in Indianapolis that featured the trades of All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and former Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner on the same day on Oct. 27.

Indianapolis continued its roster purge Tuesday with the trade of wide receiver Keenan Allen to the 49ers as the trade deadline approached. Hours later, the Colts reportedly agreed to trade wide receiver Josh Downs to the Chiefs.

But Taylor is reportedly staying put alongside Jones on an offense that looks little like it did when the Colts started the season with hopes of competing for the playoffs.

articles.title: 49ers acquire WR Keenan Allen from Colts, give up 2027 sixth-round pick
articles.summary: Allen has caught 40 passes for 351 yards and a score this season with Indianapolis.
articles.body:
Keenan Allen is headed back to California, this time to play for the San Francisco 49ers.

Allen, a Cal product best known for his time with the Chargers, is being traded midway through his first season with the Indianapolis Colts, the team announced Tuesday ahead of the deadline .

Indianapolis is receiving a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Niners in return.

The 34-year-old Allen, still facing a minimum three-game suspension following his August drunk-driving arrest , will join a San Francisco receiving corps that's been riddled by injuries. The 49ers lost Ricky Pearsall for the season this summer, as the third-year wideout underwent PCL surgery to address a knee issue that dated back to the 2025 campaign. Then, during San Francisco's season-opening win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury. Stribling, this year's No. 33 overall pick, has yet to return to game action.

As the 49ers have stormed out to a 7-1 start, fellow wideouts Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. have also dealt with injuries . Evans, navigating Achilles and ribs problems, has missed the past two games. Samuel, nursing a hamstring injury, has been out the past three. Plus, another member of the team's receiver room, Christian Kirk, has been sidelined for most of the fall. He's now on injured reserve with a meniscus issue.

Even with a shorthanded offense, quarterback Brock Purdy is playing some of his best football under head coach Kyle Shanahan. Purdy's 109.8 passer rating is the second best of his career. He leads all qualifying NFL passers this season in EPA per dropback (+0.25), per Next Gen Stats.

Purdy will surely welcome another weapon, especially considering Allen has performed relatively well in his 14th NFL season.

The six-time Pro Bowler has appeared in eight games this season, starting four and piling up 40 receptions and 351 receiving yards. He scored one touchdown for a middling Colts offense.

At 2-7, Indianapolis is currently the league's biggest deadline seller. On Oct. 27, more than a week after firing longtime general manager Chris Ballard , the Colts traded left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. They were two of the organization's longest-tenured players. The six-time All-Pro Nelson went to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. And the two-time All-Pro Buckner landed back with his old team, the 49ers , who gave up a 2027 fourth-round draft pick for the interior defensive lineman.

As for Allen's suspension, he's not expected to miss playing time while his case makes its way through the courts. So he could very well finish the 2026 season without serving a ban.

Allen, notably, is on an expiring contract. He signed a one-year deal with the Colts this summer.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Won't Be Traded by Colts Despite 'Multiple Offers,' New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are sticking with star running back Jonathan Taylor despite a 2-7 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are sticking with star running back Jonathan Taylor despite a 2-7 start to the 2026 season.

The Colts are not planning on trading Taylor ahead of the Tuesday deadline, The Ringer and Netflix's Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday.

According to Pelissero, "multiple teams offered a second-round pick and more for Taylor," but the Colts "wanted a blockbuster offer to even consider it."

The news comes after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Colts listened to an offer from the Minnesota Vikings on Daniel Jones but "did not want to move" the quarterback.

ESPN and NFL Network's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport previously reported the Colts were "open" to trading Taylor, but Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported Indianapolis was looking for a return on the level of a first-round pick.

Taylor, 27, agreed to a two-year million extension worth up to $47 million with $39 million guaranteed ahead of the 2026 season.

That new deal is set to kick in next season and keep Taylor under contract through his age-29 campaign in 2028, per Over the Cap .

After consecutive Pro Bowl seasons with at least 1,400 rushing yards in 2024 and 2025, Taylor got off to a slow start to the 2026 campaign amid struggles from Daniel Jones and the rest of the Colts offense.

Taylor had recorded 656 rushing yards and eight touchdowns through nine games to mark the fewest yards per carry of his career.

The Colts will hope for Taylor to see a resurgence as the franchise works on retooling around him this offseason.

Indianapolis began instituting change in mid-October by firing general manager Chris Ballard in the middle of his 10th season with the team.

Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said at the time the team had deliberately dismissed Ballard during the season because "waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now."

That work continued with the trades of defensive linemen DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, followed by a deal for wide receiver Keenan Allen.

Other players including quarterback Anthony Richardson could still be on the trade block given the Colts are in need of draft picks after giving up their 2027 first-rounder in last year's deal for Sauce Gardner.

The Colts will hope to solve their problems at quarterback by either replacing Jones or relying on a rebound season from the signal caller.

Keeping Taylor could be a sign the Colts are hoping to use their 2027 draft picks to retool around their star running back, and whichever quarterback starts next season into more competitive team in the near future.

Taylor, selected by the Colts in the second round of the 2020 draft, earned three Pro Bowl nods in his first six seasons with the franchise. He currently ranks second only to Edgerrin James for the most career rushing yards in Colts history.

articles.title: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins: Minnesota reunites with former QB in deal with Raiders
articles.summary: Cousins is headed back to Minnesota.
articles.body:
After watching Carson Wentz crash and burn during a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9, the Minnesota Vikings came into Tuesday with one extremely obvious goal: Get another quarterback.

The team followed through on that promise, acquiring Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein confirmed.

The Raiders will receive a 2027 third-round pick in exchange for the veteran quarterback.

The team also confirmed the move , noting it was still dependent on Cousins passing his physical.

It was the most obvious fit. Once it became clear the Vikings would be in the market for a quarterback at the trade deadline, both Cousins and Indianapolis Colts starter Daniel Jones came up as popular options, as both players spent time with the team in recent seasons.

Of that pair, Cousins has actually performed well this season. Thanks to his resurgence, the Raiders rank a surprising eighth in points per game in 2026. The team ranked dead last in that category last season.

Cousins has played a significant role in the team's offensive turnaround. The 38-year-old has thrown 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions in nine games. Only Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has more passing touchdowns this season, and he's getting MVP buzz.

Thanks to Cousins' performance, the Raiders sent signals ahead of the trade deadline suggesting they wanted to keep the veteran passer . While that could have been a ploy to increase Cousins' value, it also made some sense. At 4-5, the Raiders are still in playoff contention. Reaching the postseason in Klint Kubiak's first year would be a significant accomplishment, especially considering the team held the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

The presence of that selection — Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza — may have ultimately resulted in the team altering course and trading Cousins. The Raiders have been hesitant to thrust Mendoza into action thus far, but it was always expected he would see the field eventually in 2026. With the trade, the Raiders have signaled it's officially the Mendoza era in Las Vegas.

For the Vikings, the move should be viewed as a significant upgrade. The team's original solution at quarterback — Kyler Murray — hasn't proved to be the answer in his six starts. And after Wentz threw for just 81 yards in Week 9 — with three turnovers — it became obvious someone else needed to be brought in. With the Vikings' defense playing at an elite level, the only thing separating the team from being a legitimate Super Bowl contender was competent quarterback play.

Cousins was always the best option on the table. Given his performance and familiarity with the franchise, Cousins immediately gives the Vikings Super Bowl upside.

While Cousins is familiar with the Vikings' offense, it's unclear when he'll take the field with the team. The team's next game will take place at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

If Cousins does start for the Vikings in that game, it would mark his first start with the franchise since Week 8 of the 2023 NFL season. His opponent that week: The Packers at Lambeau Field.

Success is not a sure thing. While Cousins has played well this season, he looked like a diminished player last year. And for all his regular-season success, Cousins doesn't have the best track record in big games.

Despite that, it was a move the Vikings needed to make. Defenses like this don't come along very often, and the Vikings couldn't afford to see their season slip away thanks to miserable quarterback play.

Cousins comes with risks. He also gives the team its best chance to win the Super Bowl in 2026.
