articles.title: Seahawks’ Derick Hall’s Message to Klint Kubiak Before Raiders Game
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks edge rusher Derick Hall has a message for Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak leading into their game. The post Seahawks’ Derick Hall’...
articles.body:
Derick Hall is one of the key reasons the Seattle Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions.

The 25-year-old is one of the top young stars on a stingy defensive unit that ranks fourth in the NFL in points allowed per game. That's just a year removed after leading the Seahawks to the best defensive ranking in the NFL, allowing just 17.2 points per game.

Hall posted two sacks in the Seahawks' Super Bowl LX victory over the New England Patriots and parlayed that into a three-year, $42 million contract extension in the offseason.

Things haven't been perfect this season for Seattle as it's been an up-and-down year. They're 5-4 and in the thick of the NFC playoff race, but they've been forced to deal with key injuries to starters Sam Darnold and Zach Charbonnet. Seattle has been able to weather the storm and they've been able to pick up key victories, including handing the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss while also beating the Patriots in the season opener.

Derick Hall's Message For Former Seahawks Coordinator Klint Kubiak

Entering Week 10, they'll face off against a familiar face in the Klint Kubiak-led Las Vegas Raiders . Kubiak is obviously best known for his tenure as the offensive coordinator of the Seahawks, helping lead them to the Super Bowl last season before landing the Raiders head coaching job.

"Klint's just about ball," said Hall in a one-on-one interview with Heavy Sports. "He's a really really good guy, family man, big on his faith. Loves God, loves his family, and loves football. When you have all those three things, and you're doing it the right way and working for you, success is going to come. But Klint, man, he just does all the things the right way. He's a great offensive mind, one of the best in the game. Has all the motions, has all the movements, has all the things that can get you out of place. It's about getting the call, getting lined up, trying to execute that to the best of our ability. Because we know Klint always got some stuff up his sleeve, as we saw last year when he was here with us, man. So great offensive mind. It'll be am honor to play against him, and we're looking forward to it."

When asked if he has a certain message for his former coach, Hall keeps it modest and said he'll show his appreciation for the 39-year-old head coach before the game.

"Probably just love him, love him up, but nothing else to say," said Hall. "Just go to work."

Derick Hall Partners With Huggies For World Prematurity Day

Hall is obviously one of the stars of the Seahawks, but his background story is beyond special. The 25-year-old was born premature by four months (at 23 weeks) and was given just a 1% chance of living. Doctors told his mother that even if Hall survived, he wouldn't be able to live a normal life.

His mother fought for him and Hall ended up not only living a normal life, he emerged as a top football star with the Seahawks drafting him in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft.

The biggest message from Hall's story is one of resilience and battling through when all odds are stacked against you. It's the reason why he's partnering with Huggies leading into World Prematurity Day (Nov. 15).

"That's 100% correct," said Hall of the biggest message from his life story is being of resilience. "And more than anything, it takes a village to raise a child. The main piece for me is my mom. My mom was my advocate. Being a premie baby, you need someone to fight for. You need someone to advocate for you, so that being your mother, your father, your family, and then you have the secondary level of that, which is Huggies, and myself and my foundation. It's just so huge to have that belief, that resilience, that fight, and know that someone is fighting for you. O

"Obviously as a kid, a little infant baby, you can't realize those things, but as you begin to grow, because these hardships can last for good bit of time in the adolescent years of their lif, you begin to see who's been there for you and who's the people who's been doing the background work. Your parents advocating for yo, so that's true to us about resilience, fight, toughness, grit, connection and then just having people to fight for you, getting your parents Huggies, and then having an opportunity to do this. Which is so special to me about giving back and having this opportunity myself."

Hall details his partnership with Huggies even further and the message he's trying to spread through his foundation.

"This partnership with Huggies came about obviously partially due to my story and NICU Awareness Month," said Hall. "That's really where it all started for me. This partnership, a lot of people know my story. I was a premie, given a 1% chance to live, and Huggies has been doing the the background work for premies for years and years. When I had this opportunity to partner with them, it was a no brainer for me and my foundation, the Derick Foundation, and my family. It's just so key to have somebody fighting for you, being at bat, being combative for you and your family. It's such a hardship because being a premie parent isn't easy.

"Going through all these hardships, knowing that there's someone to show you the love, support, and connection in Huggies, and then the foundation of myself is just so huge," said Hall. "You have World Premature Day coming up on November 15. So just in that opportunity, spread that light, spread that joy, let families know what Huggies is doing for premie babies in those moments, and let them know that there are people there to support you and help you through those hardships and those hard moments. It's amazing. it's something truly special, and I'm just looking forward to continue to grow this partnership and continue to know Huggies at a deeper level, and them obviously know me at a deeper level, so it's amazing."

articles.title: Winless Chargers make first move of NFL trade deadline with AFC West partner
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are trading linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos. Here's what we know:
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have made a move after all.

Linebacker Daiyan Henley will remain in the AFC West as the Chargers plan to trade him to the Denver Broncos , according to multiple reports. It's the first trade Los Angeles is making ahead of this year's NFL trade deadline.

For weeks, there had been reports that the winless Chargers were not interested in trading away their players to recoup draft capital. After an eighth straight loss to open the year on Sunday, Nov. 8, their tune appears to have changed.

Henley, 26, was in the final year of his rookie contract with Los Angeles. The linebacker began his career with the Chargers as a third-round pick in 2023. He ends his tenure with the team that drafted him, having tallied 317 tackles, 14 tackles for a loss, 15 passes defended, five sacks and four interceptions.

Here's what the Broncos are giving up to acquire their new linebacker:

NFL trade deadline: Players on the move as Nov. 10 cutoff looms

Henley was among the most obvious tradable assets on the Chargers' roster as their season-opening losing streak continued. The fourth-year linebacker's contract expires after this season, and he has struggled to adjust to new defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary's system since Jesse Minter departed for the Ravens ' head coaching job.

The Broncos provide the change of scenery that could benefit Henley midway through the season. Under Vance Joseph, Henley could see a return to his strong coverage abilities that defined his early years in Los Angeles. That could be key for Denver's middle-of-the-field defense, as Alex Singleton has struggled in pass coverage so far this year.

articles.title: Broncos’ updated order of 2027 NFL draft picks after Daiyan Henley trade
articles.summary: Here's a look at the Broncos' projected order of 2027 draft picks following the Daiyan Henley trade.
articles.body:
After agreeing to trade a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, the Denver Broncos still have plenty of draft capital for 2027.

In addition to holding their original selections in six rounds, the Broncos also hold a seventh-round selection from the New Orleans Saints following their 2025 Devaughn Vele trade . Denver is also projected to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick for losing John Franklin-Myers and a seventh-round comp pick for losing safety P.J. Locke during NFL free agency this spring.

Additionally, if defensive coordinator Vance Joseph lands a head coach job in 2027, the Broncos would receive a third-round comp pick in 2027 and another third-round selection in 2028 as part of the NFL's Rooney Rule that rewards teams for developing minority coaches and executives.

There's no guarantee that Joseph will leave for a head coach role, though, so here's a look at the team's current projected picks as things stand now.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline tracker: Live updates on news, rumors for Kirk Cousins, Jonathan Taylor and more at 2026 deadline
articles.summary: The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline. Follow along below with the news.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching, giving teams one last chance to make deals for the postseason stretch.

In recent years, the NFL trade deadline has increased in excitement as more teams have become willing to make moves during the season. That has continued this year, as there have already been major moves as contenders aim to strengthen their rosters for the second half and the playoffs.

Thus far, the biggest trade story has been the Indianapolis Colts , who have sold a few pieces amid a disappointing season. They still have one of the biggest names available, though, as Jonathan Taylor could be traded if Indianapolis finds a team to pay its asking price.

Taylor is not the only running back in rumors, though, with Derrick Henry also facing a trade possibility if the Baltimore Ravens want to sell the impending free agent. So far, the Ravens have been unwilling to trade the star as they hope to still compete down the stretch.

The trade deadline will come and pass on Tuesday afternoon, and now that Week 9 is wrapping up, teams can focus on making deals in the final few days before the deadline.

The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline. Follow along below with the news.

Nov. 10 : The Indianapolis Colts traded WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Nov. 10 : The Los Angeles Chargers traded LB Daiyan Henry to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Nov. 10 : The Las Vegas Raiders traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick.

Nov. 10 : The Tennessee Titans traded S Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a second-round pick.

Nov. 10 : The Indianapolis Colts traded WR Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Nov. 9: The Philadelphia Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Nov. 9: The New York Jets traded S Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Nov. 9: The New Orleans Saints traded DT Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Nov. 9 : The Atlanta Falcons traded S Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick.

Nov. 4 : The Arizona Cardinals traded QB Jacoby Brissett and a fifth-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a fourth-round pick and a seventh-round pick.

Oct. 29 : The Tennessee Titans traded DT Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick.

Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded DT DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick.

Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded OG Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for third- and fifth-round picks.

Oct. 11 : The Arizona Cardinals traded WR Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans for second- and sixth-round picks.

Oct. 7 : The Philadelphia Eagles traded OG Cam Jurgens and a seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 fifth-round pick.

Sept. 30 : The Pittsburgh Steelers traded CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-round pick.

Sept. 28 : The Minnesota Vikings traded QB J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

The Chiefs are sending the Colts a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick for Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick. Kansas City is much improved this year but badly needed help in the wide receiver room, so they get the talented pending free agent in Downs.

Denver gets linebacker help in the form of Henry, sending a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick back to the Chargers in return. Los Angeles was hesitant to sell but agreed to this deal before the deadline.

The Colts received offers headlined by second-round picks, but the team opted to keep their star for the remainder of the season. Indianapolis has just two wins and is clearly in rebuild mode, making Taylor one of the few reasons to watch the team.

The Vikings get Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick, bringing the former Minnesota QB back to try and help fix the offense. Cousins spent 2018-2023 with the team, leading Minnesota to multiple playoff appearances.

The full deal sees the Titans sending Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Bills for a second-round pick. Hooker has been one of the best Titans all season, as he even intercepted Joe Burrow three times in the same game earlier in the year.

San Francisco sends Indianapolis a sixth-round pick for Allen, who will be playing for his fourth team with the 49ers. Allen is a veteran who gives the 49ers some experience down the stretch.

Vikings have yet to make call to Saints about Derek Carr

Minnesota's quarterbacking woes have brought about a host of wacky rumors, one of which links the franchise with retired hurler Derek Carr. Florio reported that Minnesota hasn't placed a call for the aging passer. He remains on New Orleans' reserved/retired list, meaning the Vikings would have to trade for him to land his services.

Tyreek Hill lurking in the shadows, per agent

Hill has yet to be medically cleared from the dislocated knee he suffered last year, but is anticipating receiving the thumbs up to return in a few weeks, according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus. That could open the door to him returning to the field as a free agent.

Cowboys considering signing Kendre Miller as RB2

The Cowboys are in the market for a new tailback after backup Tyler Goodson suffered a knee injury in Week 9. Per Archer, Dallas is looking at Miller, who was recently a casualty of waivers. The former Saints running back tallied 159 yards and two touchdowns on 57 carries this season before getting purged.

Chargers may be willing to listen to offers

Schultz reports that Los Angeles seems more "receptive" to offers in the last 24 hours and could trade players if the deal is right. While the Chargers remain the lone team in the NFL without a win, they haven't appeared interested in moving players yet.

It turns out, Cincinnati didn't want Ebiketie to mean the team loses a third-round compensatory pick, so the team backed out of the deal. The comp pick formula could end up impacting the Bengals' plans today.

Commanders 'unlikey' to make any significant moves

At 2-5-1, the Commanders' season is going in the wrong direction, but Washington does not appear inclined to make any of their players available. The Commanders have many veterans they could explore trading if they do change their mind.

Bengals acquire Arnold Ebiketie from Eagles

Philadelphia's sale continues by sending Ebiketie to Cincinnati for a sixth-round pick in 2027. The linebacker was in his first season with the Eagles after four seasons with the Falcons, producing 25 tackles in nine games for the defense.

Vikings targeting Kirk Cousins, Daniel Jones

The Vikings appear to be focusing their efforts on two former Minnesota quarterbacks in Cousins and Jones. Cousins, of course, spent many years with the Vikings and led them to the playoffs a few times, while Jones spent the latter part of the 2024 season with them even though he never appeared in a game.

Jaguars plan on keeping Brian Thomas Jr.

While Thomas has been in trade rumors for a while, Jacksonville said it will not move him before the deadline. That makes Thomas good depth for the Jaguars even though he has not performed as he did during his rookie season in 2024.

Jerry Jones expects quiet Cowboys deadline

"A lot of things happen on this last day, but I don't look for us to make a significant trade today," Jones told 103.5 The FAN on Tuesday morning. The Cowboys could use some help on defense, but they have already used many of their assets to acquire players and probably don't want to extend too much more.

After Carson Wentz's nightmare game on Monday night, the Vikings quarterback position might be the biggest need in the entire sport. With a playoff spot still in sight, Minnesota will try to salvage the season before it's too late.

Jonathan Taylor 'open' to trade, Titans don't want to trade Tony Pollard

As of Monday afternoon, Taylor is considered "open to being traded," but the Colts want to maximize the value in return, rather than "force" a trade right now, according to Schultz. As for Titans running back Tony Pollard, Schultz reports that Tennessee hasn't proven willing to move Pollard, wanting to keep Cam Ward's top offensive weapons around him.

Lions TE Sam LaPorta has made it clear he is comfortable playing elsewhere next season as he prepares for free agency, but don't expect a midseason trade. Interested teams "have gotten the impression that Detroit would like to keep" LaPorta, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports.

Jacksonville's upgrades on defense aren't done yet. The Jaguars are acquiring defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Eagles for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, per reports. The 26-year-old now joins defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates as the Jaguars' newest defensive additions ahead of the 2026 trade deadline.

In nine games this season, Davis recorded 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks. The 2022 first-round pick just signed a three-year, $78 million contract extension in March of this season.

Colts have tabled at least one offer for Josh Downs

Speaking on "The Pat McAfee Show", Schefter revealed that the Colts have received at least one offer for Downs. Per Schefter, one team offered a fourth-rounder for Downs. That wasn't enough to get Indianapolis to budge, though.

Jets deal S Andre Cisco to Lions for sixth-round pick

New York is sending Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, per Schefter. Cisco, 26, has 23 tackles, one sack and one pass deflection in nine games (four starts) this season. His contract expires at the end of the season.

Jaguars acquire DT Davon Godchaux in deal with Saints

Jacksonville bolstered its defensive line ahead of Tuesday's deadline, landing Godchaux in its second major move. The 31-year-old has been a starter for much of his career but has seen his minutes fluctuate thus far, taking just 30 percent of defensive snaps with New Orleans this season. He has 15 tackles and one tackle for loss this season.

Smith has been solid for the Jets this season, but with New York at 2-7 on the year, other teams have called to see if they could get the veteran quarterback. However, there is no evidence that the Jets are willing to part with their starting quarterback.

The pass rusher has lost opportunities this year on a bad Jets defense and would like a fresh start, but the Jets have thus far not entertained trade calls for him. McDonald is signed through 2027 thanks to his fifth-year option.

Jaguars acquire Jessie Bates from Falcons

Atlanta will get a second- and a fifth-round pick back in return. Bates is a former Pro Bowler with playoff experience from his time with the Bengals, and he becomes an upgrade in the back of the Jaguars' defense

Jonathan Taylor gave farewell speech to media

After the Colts' loss to the Cowboys, Taylor told the media how much he enjoyed playing for Indianapolis in case the team trades him. It's still unclear if the Colts will pull the trigger on trading Taylor, but this is a sign that Taylor knows it's possible.

Colts told Daniel Jones he won't be traded

With the Colts struggling, Jones' name appeared in trade rumors, but Indianapolis decided not to move the veteran quarterback. That doesn't mean that Jones will remain the Colts' starter for the rest of the season, but it does ensure he finishes the season in Indianapolis.

Giants pulled offer for Colts' Jonathan Taylor

According to Glazer, the Giants offered a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor, but have since taken back the offer. New York will now only engage in talks if the Colts' asking price comes down.

Chargers likely to hold on to key players

While the Chargers have been a disappointment this season, Los Angeles is not expected to unload before the deadline. That means that Justin Herbert, Khalil Mack and Ladd McConkey are all expected to stay in Los Angeles.

Ravens not expected to trade Derrick Henry

The Ravens' season is hanging by a thread with Lamar Jackson out, so teams have called about Henry, who is an impending free agent. For now, Baltimore has declined those offers and plan on keeping Henry for the rest of the season.

Colts turned down Daniel Jones inquiries

Despite teams making calls on Jones, Indianapolis turned down offers ahead off Sunday's game against the Cowboys. With the Colts at 2-7, though, those calls are unlikely to stop before the trade deadline passes on Tuesday afternoon.

There are no reports that the Cardinals have made Trey McBride available, but that hasn't stopped the Broncos from trying to acquire the star tight end. McBride is a Colorado native who has established himself as one of the best tight ends in the league.

Teams have contacted Colts about Daniel Jones

The season has not gone well in Indianapolis, which means Jones could be on the move to a QB-needy team. The Vikings are surely one to watch if the Colts decide to trade their starting quarterback.

All trades had to be agreed upon and submitted to the NFL office by 4 p.m. ET. There is a chance that certain deals are reported after the deadline, but as long as the calls are submitted to the office in time, then the trades will go through.

articles.title: Can Vikings still make the playoffs? What trade for Kirk Cousins means for Minnesota’s outlook
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins in back in Vikings colors. His return could spur Minnesota back into the postseason.
articles.body:
One day after seeing their offense stumble against one of football's most porous defensive units en route to defeat against the Bills , the Vikings are making major changes to their quarterback room.

Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders , dealing a third-round pick in the other direction to land its former standout. The move constitutes a minor risk for the Vikings, who have struggled to get their collection of gifted pass-catchers — namely Justin Jefferson — involved in the attack in recent weeks.

Minnesota's offensive foibles resurfaced during its 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. While the Vikings' defense performed admirably, their attack was notably more toothless, failing to mount much of a challenge against Buffalo's much-maligned backline.

While Cousins has his detractors, he should prove more capable of throwing the ball downfield than the likes of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. His familiarity with head coach Kevin O'Connell's playbook should help him surge to the top of Minnesota's QB depth chart upon arrival — a place he's more than familiar with.

With that, here's a look at how the Vikings can capitalize on Cousins' acquisition to surge to the playoffs.

Minnesota's 6-2 record belies Super Bowl contention. Its offensive exploits through nine games suggest otherwise. The Vikings are locked into a playoff spot thus far, sitting pretty at 6-2. They'll have ample adversaries vying for their spot, namely the Seahawks and the Rams .

The Vikings' postseason hopes don't entirely rest upon Cousins' broad shoulders. The Brian Flores-led defense remains elite, holding the high-octane Bills attack to a season-low in points despite failing to receive any real production from the offense. Barring poor health, Minnesota should receive enough from its backline to stay in games.

Cousins, instead, will be tasked with providing the fairy dust the Vikings' attack has desperately needed. He enjoyed a sizzling stint in Sin City, putting him on pace to tally a career-high in passing touchdowns. If he can at all rekindle that form in Minnesota — or close to it — the Vikings should be able to see out enough contests to keep their place among the NFC's elite (or scale even higher heights).

When peering at Minnesota's schedule, it looks somewhat daunting. Matchups against the Commanders and Jets should go the Vikings' way. If those results play out the way Minnesotans would envision, that would leave the Vikings with at least eight wins.

From that point, things get a little murkier. The Packers, Niners, Falcons , Panthers , Patriots , Lions and Bears all figure to be in postseason contention come the end of the season. They'll prove formidable tests for the Vikings, particularly if it takes Cousins some time to readjust to Kevin O'Connell's system.

The seventh-seed has averaged 9.6 wins since the league introduced a 17th game into its annual schedule in 2021. No team that has won more than 11 games has missed the playoffs in that stretch. While the aforementioned matchups could prove daunting, the reality is that if Minnesota wins three of those contests, it is all but assured a postseason berth — especially if some of those wins come against divisional opposition.

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 trade deadline tracker
articles.summary: Follow ongoing coverage of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, including whether or not the Seahawks make one more move.
articles.body:
We've reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it's not like we live in a "nothing happens" world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans.

For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they've pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls' trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we'll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start.

Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season?

Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder.

Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block?

No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn't fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he's not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart.

Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in?

Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed's injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O'Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets' Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch.

When does the NFL trade deadline window close?

Josh Downs is going from the Indianapolis Colts to the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs will give up a fourth- and fifth-rounder and also get a seventh-rounder in return.

The Denver Broncos land Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a 2027 fourth- and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

Kirk Cousins is going to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-rounder , which means the Seahawks will not face Cousins this Sunday. Fernando Mendoza figures to make his first NFL start.

The Buffalo Bills are acquiring Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick in exchange for a second-round pick.

The 49ers are trading a 2027 sixth-rounder to the Colts for veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen.

The Eagles are trading pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick. UPDATE: No they're not .

WHOA! The Jaguars just traded for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis , giving up a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second.

The New York Jets have dealt safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-rounder.

The New Orleans Saints have agreed to trade defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-rounder, which could become a 2027 sixth-rounder.

articles.title: Fire sale continues for Texans rivals as Titans move top DB to contender
articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons was one of two defenders capable of making it a game for the Tennessee Titans against the Texans each season. Now, both are gone before Houst...
articles.body:
Jeffery Simmons was one of two defenders capable of making it a game for the Tennessee Titans against the Houston Texans each season. He was shipped off to the Chicago Bears two weeks ago for two first-round picks.

The other star player? Well, he's on his way to Buffalo for the remainder of the 2026 season.

The Buffalo Bills have agreed to trade a 2027 second-round pick to the Titans in exchange for safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick. Hooker, a former standout at Iowa, moves on to a contender for only the second time in his career.

A quality defensive back, Hooker had hit his stride under first-year head coach Robert Saleh in 2026, leading the NFL with five interceptions, along with 52 tackles and six pass breakups. On a one-win team that seems more content to be in the running for the No. 1 overall pick, Tennessee believed it was best to ship him out and no lose him in free agency to nothing more than a compensatory pick down the line.

A multi-purpose defender, Hooker roves between the strong and free safety roles, often playing whichever position the other safety can't. Most recently, he took over as the free safety last season, becoming a must-see in coverage on downfield plays.

The price was perhaps so high due to the years left on the deal. Hooker is under contract through 2028, so his contract won't come up in conversations until after that season. His salary cap hit of roughly $12 million for 2026 is pretty team-friendly compared to other safeties in the NFL.

Buffalo had been in the market for a safety since the release of former Texans starter C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who was released after six games with the team and a suspension. Gardner-Johnson only lasted three games with the Texans before being released amid a 0-3 start.

The Texans close out the regular season at home against the Titans in January. Given that both the Colts and Titans have been big-time sellers, it seems like Houston is locked in for no worse than second in the divisional standings this season.

articles.title: Colts reportedly trading WR Josh Downs to Chiefs after receiver requested a trade
articles.summary: Downs is the second wide receiver dealt by the Colts on Tuesday following Keenan Allen's move to the 49ers.
articles.body:
Josh Downs is the latest player to leave Indianapolis after the Colts reportedly dealt the wide receiver to the Kansas City Chiefs, according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .

Per Tom Pelissero , the Chiefs, who are also acquiring a 2027 seventh-round draft pick, are sending a fourth- and fifth-round pick in 2027 back to Indianapolis.

The 25-year-old Downs, who is set to become a free agent in the offseason, requested a trade away from Indianapolis. His move follows the exits of guard Quenton Nelson , defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen , who were shipped out with the team off to a 2-7 start.

Downs posted on social media after reports of the trade broke and was very relieved the matter was finally over.

Downs was the Colts' third-round pick in the 2023 draft out of North Carolina. He recorded 1,574 receiving yards on 140 catches and seven touchdowns over his first two seasons.

This season, with Alec Pierce out due to injury, Downs led the Colts with 354 receiving yards and 57 targets.

The addition of the two picks will give the Colts a total of 13 in the 2027 draft. They still do not have a first-round selection after trading it to the New York Jets last season in the Sauce Gardner deal.

With Allen and Downs leaving, the Colts added Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to their wide receiver room on Tuesday.

articles.title: Broncos trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley
articles.summary: According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round p...
articles.body:
According to ESPN's lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley.

Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections.

Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos' defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly.

The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason.

I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He's an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos.

Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos' third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him.

With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

articles.title: Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings were desperate to make a trade for a quarterback before the deadline after Monday night’s tough loss to the Buffalo Bills at home. Late...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings were desperate to make a trade for a quarterback before the deadline after Monday night's tough loss to the Buffalo Bills at home. Later in the day on Tuesday, they did just that , reuniting with a familiar face in the process.

"Blockbuster! The Raiders are trading four-time Pro Bowl QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for their 2027 third-round pick," reported NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer on X, formerly Twitter.

The move reunites the Vikings with Cousins after he spent multiple seasons there with head coach Kevin O'Connell, finding considerable success in the process. Minnesota's defense has been elite this year but its offense has stumbled, with neither Kyler Murray nor Carson Wentz finding consistent success under center, making it clear that the team had to make a change before the deadline.

Meanwhile, this move now officially hands the keys to number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas. Mendoza has yet to make a start at the NFL level, but that will now change after he spent half of his rookie season learning behind Cousins.

Cousins got off to a hot start to the year in Las Vegas, and although he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, he is still a competent veteran quarterback who should provide an upgrade for the Vikings immediately at the position.

In any case, the Vikings will next hit the field on Sunday vs the Green Bay Packers, while Mendoza looks slated to make his first NFL start the same day vs the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Malik Willis Injured, Latest Rumors on Dolphins QB's Timeline to Return from Groin Issue
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins will be without starting quarterback Malik Willis for at least a month.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins will be without starting quarterback Malik Willis for at least a month.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported that Willis has been battling a groin injury that developed into a core muscle injury, so he will be placed on injured reserve. The injury is not considered season-ending, but he will miss at least the next four weeks. Second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will make his first career start on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.
